newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-RANGERS GAIN SOME BREATHING ROOM IN AL WEST.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-RANGERS GAIN SOME BREATHING ROOM IN AL WEST.

text.p: The Texas Rangers appear to have finally stopped the bleeding and gave themselves a bit of breathing room atop the American League West with a 4-1 victory over the California Angeles on Sunday.
Juan Gonzalez and Dean Palmer hit fourth-inning homers as the Rangers won back-to-back games after snapping a five-game slide Saturday night.
Texas moved two games ahead of Seattle, which had a 10-game winning streak snapped, after losing eight games in the standings to the hard charging Mariners in nine days.

"The ballclub is starting to feel good about itself again," manager Johnny Oates said. "Who knows what will happen in the last six games? Nobody said it was going to be easy. But nobody said it was going to be this hard, either."
Ken Hill (16-10), who had lost three of his four September starts, gave up eight hits and struck out eight in his seventh complete game of the season.
Gonzalez hit his 47th homer in the fourth off Jason Dickson (1-4) and Palmer hit his 37th homer for a 2-0 lead.

In the eighth, Palmer singled to centre off Mike Holtz, went to third on a double by Mickey Tettleton and scored on a sacrifice fly by Kevin Elster. Gonzalez added an RBI single in the ninth with his third hit of the game.

In Seattle, Mark McGwire hit a pair of upper-deck homers, including a grand slam in an eight-run fifth inning, as the Oakland Athletics built a 10-run lead and held on for a 13-11 victory that slowed the surging Mariners.
The loss, Seattle's first since September 11, dropped them 1 1/2 games behind Baltimore in the wild card race.

McGwire launched his 51st and 52nd homers, both in the fifth inning, to stake Oakland to a 13-3 lead. He is the 12th American Leaguer to homer twice in the same inning and tied for the 11th-highest home run total in major-league history.
The Mariners, who have scored 88 runs in their last 11 games, replied with seven runs in the bottom of the fifth, capped by Dave Hollins' two-run single.
Reliever Mike Mohler (6-3) got the win, despite allowing a run in the sixth. Terry Mulholland (5-3), who surrendered five runs and five hits in 2 1/3 innings, took the loss.
In New York, Paul O'Neill's sacrifice fly scored Derek Jeter, snapping a seventh-inning tie and lifting the Yankees to a 4-3 victory over the Boston Red Sox.
The win reduced New York's magic number for clinching the AL East title to four. Any number of New York wins and Baltimore losses totalling four puts the Yanks over the top.
Mariano Rivera (8-3) allowed one hit and struck out three in two scoreless innings for the win. John Wetteland notched his league-leading 42nd save.
Aaron Sele (6-11) went the distance for Boston, allowing four runs and 10 hits.
The Yankees erased a 3-1 deficit in the fifth when Bernie Williams drove a two-run triple off the right-field wall.

In Baltimore, Todd Zeile and Rafael Palmeiro each drove in two runs and Scott Erickson won his fifth straight decision as the Orioles maintained their lead in the wild card race with a 5-4 triumph over the Toronto Blue Jays.

Roberto Alomar's two-out RBI single in the seventh snapped a 4-4 tie and the Orioles hung on for the win. However they were unable to gain any ground on the first-place Yankees, who they trail by four games.
Erickson (13-11) allowed four runs and eight hits -- seven for extra bases -- over seven innings for the win. Reliever Huck Flener (2-2) took the loss.

In Chicago, Alex Fernandez threw a five-hitter for his sixth complete game and Robin Ventura hit a three-run homer to cap a four-run sixth inning as the White Sox kept their slim wild-card hopes alive with a 5-1 win over the Minnesota Twins.
The White Sox remained three games behind Baltimore in the wild card chase.
Fernandez (15-10) did not walk a batter and struck out seven. He surrendered only a solo home run to Chuck Knoblauch in the sixth inning. Scott Aldred (6-9) took the loss.

In Cleveland, Manny Ramirez's fielder's choice in the seventh inning tied the score and a throwing error by shortstop David Howard on the play allowed the go-ahead run as the Indians rallied for a 6-5 win over the Kansas City Royals.

Jason Jacome (0-4), who relieved starter Chris Haney in the seventh with a 5-3 lead, took the loss. Jack McDowell (13-9) won his third straight start despite giving up five runs and seven hits in seven innings.
Kenny Lofton went 3-for-3 and scored twice for the Indians, who have won 12 of their last 14 games.
In Milwaukee, Bob Higginson's RBI single highlighted a four-run ninth inning as the Detroit Tigers rallied past the Brewers, 7-5.
Detroit won for just the third time in 94 games when trailing after eight innings.
Reliever Mike Fetters (3-3), who was rocked in the ninth, suffered the loss, blowing his sixth save in 36 chances. Jose Lima (5-6) pitched 1 2/3 scoreless innings for the win.
